recipes.name: Pudding Breeze
ingredients_raw: 3 cups frozen whipped topping (Cool Whip®), thawed
3 (3.9 ounce) packages instant chocolate pudding mix

steps.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Crumble flour and margarine together. Blend well. Press mixture into the bottom of a 9x13 inch pan. Bake 15 minutes at 375 degrees F (190 degrees C) and let cool.
In a mixing bowl, cream cream cheese and sugar together. Stir 2 cups whipped topping into the mixture; whip together and spread evenly over cooled crust.
Mix the pudding mix with 5 cups milk (do not follow directions on box). Pour this mixture over the second layer and top with remainder of dairy whipped topping. Refrigerate and serve chilled.

raw_recipe.headline: Pudding Breeze
raw_recipe.description: This dessert is always a hit at pot luck dinners and holiday gatherings. It is very easy to make. You can substitute any type of instant pudding for chocolate.

review.reviewBody: This is an easy and delicious dessert. I have a friend who also adds 8oz. of finely chopped pecans to the flour and butter which is also very good.

Everyone loved this dessert! I made it for St Patrick’s Day so I used 2 pkgs pistachio pudding and took about one cup of the milk and added 1 pkg white chocolate pudding. I layered the pistachio then swirled the chocolate on top. Added the top layer of cool whip. For decoration I drizzled chocolate ice cream topping and pieces of Andes Candies then sprinkled graham cracker crumbs over all. Big hit!!!

Fantastic dessert! In the cream cheese layer, I use three 8 oz cartons and increase the whipped topping to one carton of zero sugar cool whip. I also use a splenda-cornstarch mixture for the powdered sugar. Instead of regular chocolate pudding, I use sugar free chocolate fudge pudding. These substitutions add body and extra flavor to the dessert. It is still scrumptious! The sugar decreases to 16g per serving for 12 servings making it more diabetic friendly.

This is really, really good! I think the serving size is incorrect. I halved this recipe and made in an 8x8 glass dish. It fit perfectly and took exactly one 8oz tub of whipped topping for the entire recipe. Also, when I cut this recipe in half it then called for 1 1/2 boxes of pudding. I had to figure out how much half a box of pudding was, so I measured it. There are approx 7 Tablespoons in a box, so 1 1/2 boxes of pudding = 1 box + 3 1/2 Tablespoons...that's how I did it anyway, and it turned out perfect. It was still a little soft after chilling for two hours, but after about four hours it was perfectly firm. I will definitely make this again.

So easy to make which is my kind of dessert. I made it with 1/3 less fat cream cheese, low-fat milk, and sugar-free pistachio pudding mix since one of our guest was diabetic and another on a diet. They all loved it and were happy they could eat dessert. Great cool dessert for a warm day.

Was DELISH!! We used 3 small boxes of instant vanilla pudding instead of the chocolate it called for and still turned out amazing! So simple! Was worried about not making the pudding by the box and just using 5 cups of milk...was the perfect tho!!

I used chocolate pudding...added 1/2 cups of crushed walnuts to mix....and then after pouring the pudding mix into a pan, I topped it with sliced bananas. Put it in the refrigerator for 3-4 hous. Right before serving, I topped it with Cool Whip and sprinkled chocolate Jimmies over it for a special effect. You can use any kind of pudding. Everyone loved it!
CC/Florida

This seems to be identical to a recipe my mom has labeled as "Pistachio Mousse," and calls for pistachio pudding. This stuff is simple, but tastes great! Like a whipped cheesecake crossed with a cream pie, all on a shortbread cookie crust. I've tried a few different variations, including banana, butterscotch, and chocolate, but pistachio is still my favorite (and I'm not even a big pistachio person). As an added bonus, the spring green color makes it a good pick for St. Patrick's Day or Easter!

I made this yesterday and had to make substitutions with adding gluten free flour and xantham gum for the crust in order to make it gluten free for my daughter with Celiac Disease. It was absolutely wonderful and I will be making it again for church potlucks. Thanks for an easy treat.

Everyone loved it. Used pistachio pudding this time. Pretty color for Easter. Next time I am going to use chocolate pudding & slice some bananas into it. Had a problem serving it. Crust stuck to the bottom so next time I will spray the bottom of the pan with Pam. It's a keeper.
This a really great recipe, my boyfriend loves it. I added 1 cup of walnuts in the crust its sooo good that way if u love nuts like i do!!!
My wedding party loved it.

I N S T A N T pudding!!!!!!!
Heaven in a bowl!
Very easy and tastes great. I've made pistachio, lemon and butterscotch. Pistachio is my favorite!
This is sooo good!! I made it with chocolate pudding and put in a 9 inch pie shell which was probably too small for this but it looked nice and pretty. :)

My MIL saw this recipe in the newspaper 30 years ago. The dessert was titled, "Better than Tom Selleck." In any case, this was easy to make, and rich tasting. It worked great for a potluck. I would make this again for family or a potluck.

My Mother-in-law made this many years ago (with a different name) in both the chocolate version and the pistachio. They were both very good. (She always added walnuts to the crust and sometimes sprinkled them on top.) To "jmellas", is it possible that you picked up the "cook and serve" kind of pudding rather than the "instant", by accident? This happened to me once (only in the reverse) since the boxes looked extremely similar. This would explain why your pudding layer remained a "soupy mess". Otherwise I don't see how the pudding layer would not have firmed up a bit. I hope this lends some insight on what might have happened.

What did i do wrong.? Mixing the pudding with milk never hardened...it was a soupy mess, much less ever being able to spread the extra whipped cream on top. I tried adding cornstarch to salvage the dessert but to no avail. I re read the recipe and reviews to try and figure out what i did wrong. Too bad the picture looks sooo good. What happened?

i have used this recipe for years I called it Kathys delicious dessert as i got it from a friend named Kathy of course..Imagine my surprise when I went out to a local restaurant and they had it in butterscotch flavor on their menu for dessert..I have always added ground nuts to the crust and the restruuant had it made up as a pie..but same recipe...
